back: Initiate Project or Phase; Integrate and Align Project Plans; Plan Sourcing Strategy; Manage Project Execution; Manage Quality Assurance; Manage Project Knowledge; Monitor and Control Project Performance; Assess and Implement Changes; Close Project or Phase.
Officially authorizes the project and gives the project manager authority over resources by creating the project charter. Older name: Develop Project Charter.

front: Outputs of Initiate Project or Phase
back: Project charter and assumption log.
Consolidates and aligns all plan components into one project management plan. Older name: Develop Project Management Plan.
Decides whether to use internal or external resources and how outside sources will be selected and contracted. Older name: Plan Procurement Management.
The technique for deciding whether work is better done internally or purchased from outside.
Brings in missing expertise and transfers delivery risk to the supplier. Often cheaper for common goods or services.
More control and oversight of deliverables, and tighter integration with strategy. Often cheaper when substantial new innovation is needed.
Leading and performing the work in the plan and implementing approved changes. Older name: Direct and Manage Project Work.
Deliverables, work performance data, issue log, change requests, plan and document updates.
Ensuring project processes are performed in a manner consistent with stakeholder expectations. Output: quality reports.
Assurance: the process (standards, compliance, audits). Control: the deliverables (testing, specifications, defects).
Using existing knowledge and creating new knowledge to achieve objectives and contribute to organizational learning. Output: lessons learned register.
Formal and systematic knowledge that can be codified in words, pictures or numbers: manuals, procedures. Shared through documents and databases.
Personal knowledge embedded in a person's mind: experience, insight, know-how. Hard to articulate; shared through interaction.
The project document that records knowledge gained during a project, phase or iteration so it can improve future performance.
Tracking, reviewing and reporting overall progress against the plan. Output: work performance reports. Older name: Monitor and Control Project Work.
The act of measuring something influences behavior, so choose metrics carefully.
A measure that shows data but gives no useful information for making decisions.
Two things moving together does not prove that one causes the other.
The tendency to look for and see information that supports your existing point of view.
Managing project changes from start to finish: reviewing requests and adjusting plans. Older name: Perform Integrated Change Control.

front: When are changes formally controlled in a predictive project?
back: Once baselines are established.
A formally established group that reviews, evaluates, approves, defers or rejects changes and records and communicates the decisions.

front: First step when a change is requested
back: Document it and assess its impact (schedule, cost, risk, other areas) before any decision.

front: Three possible decisions on a change request
back: Approved, deferred or rejected. The decision is recorded in the change log.

front: Change management plan vs configuration management plan
back: Change management plan: sets up the CCB, its authority and the change control system. Configuration management plan: defines which artifacts are tracked and controlled, and how.

front: How are changes handled in adaptive projects?
back: Through backlog management. A change becomes a backlog item and is prioritized; low priority means deferred, not added means rejected.
Finalizing all activities for a project, phase, release, iteration or contract, whether successful or not.

front: Outputs of Close Project or Phase
back: Final product, service or result transition; final report; lessons learned register updates; organizational process asset updates.

front: Must a cancelled project be closed?
back: Yes. Closing applies to terminated projects too, and includes documenting the reasons.
Light governance with clear boundaries, where an agile team decides its own processes, priorities and problem-solving.
